thread.title: These 12 T. Rowe Price mutual funds beat the S&P 500 in 2017

author: Holden Wilen
title: These 12 T. Rowe Price mutual funds beat the S&P 500 in 2017
text: – Reporter, Baltimore Business Journal Feb 7, 2018, 1:28pm EST Driven by tech giants like Amazon, Apple, Alphabet and Facebook , a dozen T. Rowe Price Group portfolio managers beat the S&P 500 in 2017. The total is twice the number of portfolio managers that beat the closely watched index last year. Across the board, Baltimore-based T. Rowe Price's mutual funds posted gains, but the biggest returns came from those invested in so-called "FAANG" stocks — Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix and Alphabet's Google . In a year when the stock market set records, the group of tech giants all had big years. The stock market surged in President Donald Trump 's first year in part because of his promises to cut regulations and taxes. Despite an ongoing investigation into the Trump campaign's possible ties to Russian meddling in U.S. elections and a failure by Congress to overhaul former President Barack Obama 's health care law, the market continually reached new highs. Corporations got a big win in December when Congress passed the long-promised tax reform bill that included cutting the corporate income tax rate from 35 percent to 21 percent. The Dow Jones industrial average ended 2017 up 25 percent and added 5,000 points to reach 24,000 — the biggest annual-points gain in history. The Nasdaq composite ended the year up almost 29 percent and the Standard & Poor's 500 index was up about 21.8 percent. For T. Rowe Price, the markets helped the money manager's assets under management grow 22 percent to $991.1 billion as of Dec. 31. "This was a very good quarter and year for T. Rowe Price (NASDAQ: TROW), our clients, and our stockholders," CEO William J. Stromberg said in a statement last month as the company reported its fourth-quarter earnings. Two of portfolio managers who beat the S&P 500 were nominated for Fund Manager of the Year awards by Morningstar: Larry Puglia , manager of the Blue Chip Growth Fund; and Henry Ellenbogen, manager of the New Horizons Fund. Here are the 12 U.S. funds that beat the S&P 500 in 2017. Science and Technology Fund: Ken W. Allen's $5.4 billion fund had the biggest return of any fund with a 39.2 percent return. The fund focuses on technology companies with potential for real earnings and revenue growth and who are leading or growing market share. The fund's largest holdings include Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB), and Altaba Inc. (NASDAQ: AABA). Blue Chip Growth Fund: Puglia managed the fund to a 36.6 percent return that beat the S&P 500 by more than 14 points. The $45.8 billion fund invests in companies with long-term capital growth. Its largest holdings are in Amazon, Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), Facebook, and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT). New America Growth Fund: The $4.4 billion fund managed by Justin P. White had a 34.6 percent return. The fund invests in U.S. companies in sectors of the economy that are the fastest growing or have the greatest growth potential. Its largest holdings include Amazon, Microsoft, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) and Facebook. Growth Stock Fund: The $51.7 billion fund managed by Joseph B. Fath had a 33.6 percent return in 2017. The fund seeks long-term capital growth through investments in companies that have superior earnings and cash flow growth, and that can sustain earnings momentum even during economic slowdowns. Its biggest holdings include Apple, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft. Media and Telecommunications Fund: Paul D. Greene managed the $4.9 billion fund to a 32.99 percent return. The fund invests in companies involved with publishing, movies, cable TV, telephones, cellular services, technology and equipment. Amazon, Alibaba Group Holding (NYSE: BABA), Facebook and Priceline (NASDAQ: PCLN) are among its biggest holdings. New Horizons Fund: Ellenbogen's $21.9 billion fund is known for investing in startups before they become well known and eventually go public. The fund had a 31.5 percent return and beat the S&P 500 by about 9.7 percentage points. The largest holdings are in Vail Resorts (NYSE: MTN), SS&C Technologies Holdings (NASDAQ: SSNC), CBOE Global Markets (NASDAQ: CBOE) and Burlington Stores Inc. (NYSE: BURL). Tax-Efficient Equity Fund: The $287 million fund managed by Donald J. Peters had a 29.1 percent return. The fund seeks to maximize after-tax growth of capital by investing primarily in mid-size and small companies. Its largest holdings include Amazon, Facebook and Alphabet. Health Sciences Fund: After being among T. Rowe Price's worst-performing funds last year, the fund beat the S&P 500 in 2017 with a 28 percent return. Ziad Bakri manages the $11.7 billion fund, which invests in pharmaceuticals, health care companies, product and device providers and biotechnology firms. The fund's largest holdings are UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH); Becton, Dickinson & Co. (NYSE: BDX); Intuitive Surgical (NASDAQ: ISRG) and Vertex Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: VRTX). Mid-Cap Growth Fund: The $30 billion fund managed by Brian W.H. Berghuis had a 24.9 percent return. The fund invests in medium-sized companies with a potential for above-average earnings growth that have successfully weathered the start-up years. Its largest holdings are in Teleflex Inc. (NYSE: TFX), Textron Inc. (NYSE: TXT) and Microchip Technology Inc . (NASDAQ: MCHP). Diversified Mid-Cap Growth Fund: Managed by Donald J. Peters and Donald J. Easley, the fund had a 24.7 percent return. The $856.6 million fund invests in the common stocks of mid-cap companies whose earnings are expected to grow at a faster rate than the average company. Its largest holdings include Ross Stores Inc. (NASDAQ: ROST), Microchip Technlogy and Fiserv Inc . (NASDAQ: FISV). Capital Opportunity Fund: The $615.2 million fund managed by Ann M. Holcomb, Jason B. Polun and Thomas H. Watson recorded a 23.7 percent return. The fund seeks to provide long-term capital growth by investing primarily in U.S. common stocks and weights each sector approximately the same as the S&P 500. Its biggest holdings are Microsoft, Apple and Alphabet. QM U.S. Small-Cap Growth Equity Fund: Sudhir Nanda managed the fund to a 22.1 percent return. The $5.96 billion fund seeks to provide long-term capital growth by investing in small companies. The fund has holdings in companies like Teledyne Technologies Inc. (NYSE: TDY), Coherent Inc. (NASDAQ: COHR) and Take-Two Interactive Software Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO).
